findings.claim: PRC annual facilitation quota: each person may settle FX and each DOMESTIC individual may buy FX up to USD 50,000 equivalent per year with ID only; above-quota transactions need transaction documents.
findings.locator: Hui Fa [2020] No. 14, Art. 54–55 (also Hui Fa [2007] No. 1, Art. 2)
findings.note: Scope matters: the purchase side of the quota is for domestic individuals (境内个人). Overseas individuals purchase against income/source documents (see V03) unless they hold a foreigner permanent-residence ID (V04). Whether a US citizen is domestic or overseas depends on residence — see V02.

findings.topic: PRC classification of a US citizen
findings.claim: A foreign national who has been continuously resident in the PRC for one year or more counts as a domestic individual (境内个人) under PRC FX rules; below one year the person is an overseas individual (境外个人).
findings.locator: State Council Order No. 532, Art. 52(2)
findings.note: This classification decides which purchase/remittance rulebook applies (quota vs source-docs). The user's residence duration is unknown here, so no route is asserted as applicable to any private balance.

findings.claim: Overseas individuals convert lawful RMB current-account income earned in China (e.g., employment pay) into FX at a bank with valid ID plus transaction-bearing source-of-funds materials that include a tax voucher (税务凭证); the bank then handles the outward current-account remittance under its document rules.
findings.locator: Hui Fa [2020] No. 14, Art. 59 ¶1 (quoted verbatim by SAFE Tianjin S01; remittance side: Art. 65)
findings.note: This is the central lawful 'get money out' path for documented income: FX purchase against proof of lawful income (incl. tax voucher), then account remittance with ID (Art. 65).

findings.claim: Overseas individuals who hold a Foreigner's Permanent Residence ID (外国人永久居留身份证) use the annual facilitation quota for FX purchases.
findings.locator: Hui Fa [2020] No. 14, Art. 59 ¶2 (in gazette S06) + SAFE Tianjin 2024-06-21 Q&A
findings.note: Statements that ANY overseas individual automatically enjoys the USD 50,000 purchase quota go beyond this text; such wording in older repository summaries is tracked in FL06.

findings.claim: Domestic individuals: FX-account remittance for current account up to USD 50,000 equivalent same day needs ID only (above: transaction documents); FX cash remittance up to USD 10,000 same day needs ID (above: customs-stamped declaration or original withdrawal slip plus documents). Overseas individuals: FX-account remittance needs valid ID; FX cash remittance up to USD 10,000 same day needs ID (above: customs-stamped declaration or original withdrawal slip).
findings.locator: Hui Fa [2020] No. 14, Art. 64–65 (same structure in Hui Fa [2007] No. 1, Art. 14–15)
findings.note: USD 50,000 here is a daily document-free threshold for outward remittance of FX already held — not a lifetime or annual cap on transfers, and not a tax.

findings.claim: An overseas individual may reconvert previously exchanged but UNUSED RMB back to FX with ID plus the original exchange slip (兑换水单) within 24 months of exchange; without the slip, only same-day conversions up to USD 500 equivalent (USD 1,000 at domestic-offshore locations before departure) are ID-only.
findings.locator: Hui Fa [2020] No. 14, Art. 60 (quoted verbatim by SAFE Tianjin 2026-09-17; also in gazette S06)
findings.note: Scope matters: this is a narrow reconversion rule for previously exchanged unused RMB — NOT a general USD 500/day allowance to convert any RMB. Older pages that generalized it are tracked in FL06.

findings.claim: Individuals must not split transactions (分拆) to evade the facilitation-quota or truthfulness requirements. Lending your quota triggers a risk warning, then watch-list (关注名单) status on repetition; borrowing others' quota puts you on the watch list directly; listing lasts the year of listing plus the following 2 years, during which all FX settlement/purchase requires transaction documents.
findings.locator: Hui Fa [2020] No. 14, Art. 62–63 (also Art. 47 for service trade)
findings.note: Structuring payments to stay under thresholds is restricted on the PRC side; on the US side cash structuring is separately prohibited (see V23).

findings.topic: PRC bank refusal — get it in writing
findings.claim: Banks must reasonably review transaction documents for personal current-account FX, may refuse transactions that violate FX rules or whose authenticity is doubtful, and must state the refusal reason accurately and provide the appeal channel.
findings.locator: Hui Fa [2020] No. 14, Art. 68
findings.note: Supports the repo's advice to ask the bank for the specific reason (documents, FX category, tax certificate vs tax assessment) in writing.

findings.topic: PRC tax-filing gate on large service payments
findings.claim: Outward service-trade payments above USD 50,000 equivalent by domestic institutions AND individuals require prior tax-filing (税务备案) procedures, and the bank verifies the tax filing form.
findings.note: Applies to service-trade payments (a business payment category), not to personal remittances of one's own funds; do not read it as a general tax on remittance.

findings.claim: FX cash withdrawal from a bank up to USD 10,000 equivalent same day: ID only; above that: ID plus withdrawal-purpose evidence with prior SAFE filing (提取外币现钞备案表). FX cash deposits and cash-convert settlements: up to USD 10,000 same day handled per identity/document rules; above requires customs-stamped declaration or the original withdrawal slip.
findings.locator: Hui Fa [2020] No. 14, Art. 86–88; supersession clause in the issuing notice; Hui Fa [2007] No. 1, Art. 30–31 for the earlier USD 5,000 deposit figure
findings.note: The 2007 Rules state a USD 5,000 same-day deposit threshold (Art. 31); the 2020 Guidelines (Art. 87) state USD 10,000, and the 2020 notice says prior provisions inconsistent with it are governed by it. Bank practice confirmation remains a customer question (FL10).

findings.claim: Carrying foreign currency INTO China above USD 5,000 equivalent requires a written customs declaration (and any second-or-later crossing in a short period requires it regardless of amount). Carrying FX OUT: amounts between USD 5,000 and 10,000 beyond the recorded inbound amount require a bank-issued Carry Permit for Foreign Exchange (携带外汇出境许可证); above USD 10,000 (for qualifying destinations) requires a SAFE-issued permit.
findings.locator: Hui Fa [2020] No. 14, Art. 89 (bank/SAFE permit system also in Hui Fa [2007] No. 1, Art. 5)
findings.note: PRC-side carry rules; the US-side report is separate (V23).

findings.claim: PRC FX penalties (statutory maxima): evading FX controls (逃汇) — fine up to 30% of the amount, or 30% up to the equivalent amount if serious, criminal liability possible; illegal FX arbitrage via false documents (非法套汇) — same 30% structure; private/improper buying-selling or brokering FX in large amounts — warning, confiscation of gains, fine up to 30%, 30%+ if serious, criminal liability; operating settlement/sale FX business without approval — confiscation of gains plus 1–5× gains if gains ≥ CNY 500,000, or CNY 500,000–2,000,000 if no/low gains, license suspension/revocation, criminal liability; carrying FX across the border in violation — warning plus fine up to 20% of the amount.
findings.locator: State Council Order No. 532, Art. 39, 40, 45, 46, 42
findings.note: Arithmetic illustration only (not a forecast): a 30% fine on USD 400,000 is USD 120,000. These are maxima applied case by case; 2020 Guidelines violations are punished via the same Regulations (S06, Art. 188).

findings.claim: PRC policy imposes no restriction in principle on current-account international payments and transfers; current-account FX income may be retained or sold, and current-account payments are made with valid documents.
findings.locator: State Council Order No. 532, Art. 5, 12–14
findings.note: A policy principle — individual transactions still require identity and authenticity documents (V03, V05).

findings.claim: PRC individual income tax: a person domiciled in China or present ≥183 days in a tax year is a resident and taxed on worldwide income; comprehensive income (wages etc.) is taxed at 3%–45% progressive rates with a CNY 60,000 annual standard deduction (non-residents: CNY 5,000/month); interest, dividends, property rental/transfer and incidental income are taxed at a flat 20%.
findings.locator: PRC IIT Law, Art. 1, 3, 6 (2018 amendment)
findings.note: Tax attaches to INCOME, not to the act of currency conversion (V16). Whether this user's balance is taxed, already taxed, or in which category is unknown (FL05).

findings.claim: PRC residents may credit foreign income tax paid against PRC tax on foreign-source income, capped at the PRC tax computed on that income under the IIT Law.
findings.locator: PRC IIT Law, Art. 7
findings.note: The US–China treaty also obliges the residence state to give a credit for the other state's tax (treaty Art. 22, per S17 front matter).

findings.topic: Conversion-penalty layer — is there a PRC tax on converting?
findings.claim: In the PRC instruments reviewed for this check (State Council Order No. 532; Hui Fa [2007] No. 1; Hui Fa [2020] No. 14) no standalone tax on the act of currency conversion was located — those instruments impose identity, document, quota and penalty rules instead. Any PRC tax due follows the underlying income (V14), not the conversion itself.
findings.locator: Absence check across S04, S05, S06 (full texts re-read this session)
findings.note: An absence claim is limited to the instruments read; it is not proof that no tax exists in any circumstance. The source and tax history of any private balance remain unknown (FL05). The root landing page states this same careful wording.

findings.claim: US citizens and resident aliens living abroad are taxed on worldwide income; a foreign earned income exclusion may apply if the bona fide residence test or the 330-day physical presence test is met, with amounts adjusted annually for inflation (fetched page lists $107,600 for 2020 through $120,000 for 2023).
findings.locator: IRS 'Foreign earned income exclusion' (page 1)
findings.note: Later-year exclusion amounts (2024–2026) are NOT on the fetched page and were not re-verified here — left blank (FL03). Repatriate's $132,900 figure is therefore not re-confirmed by this session.

findings.topic: US currency-gain rule on personal conversions
findings.claim: Under 26 U.S.C. §988, gains or losses on foreign-currency transactions are ordinary income/loss, and disposing of nonfunctional currency (including bank deposits) is a §988 transaction — BUT for individuals, personal transactions are outside §988, and in a personal disposal no gain is recognized due to exchange-rate movement unless the gain would exceed $200.
findings.note: The repo's §988(e)(2) statement matches the statutory text ($200 threshold). Amounts above $200, or non-personal transactions, need real tax computation — none is done here.

findings.claim: A US person with a financial interest in, or signature/other authority over, foreign financial accounts must file the FBAR (FinCEN Form 114) if the aggregate value exceeded USD 10,000 at any time during the calendar year; due April 15 with automatic extension to October 15; account income is irrelevant; civil and/or criminal penalties apply, with civil maxima adjusted annually for inflation.
findings.locator: IRS FBAR page + 31 CFR 1010.350 (S12)
findings.note: Specific current civil penalty DOLLAR maxima are inflation-adjusted and were not re-fetched for this pass — left blank (FL04).

findings.claim: Form 8938 thresholds for specified foreign financial assets: living in the US — unmarried/married-filing-separate more than $50,000 at year end or $75,000 at any time; married filing jointly more than $100,000/$150,000. Living abroad — unmarried more than $200,000/$300,000; married filing jointly more than $400,000/$600,000. Filing Form 8938 does not relieve FBAR duties.
findings.locator: IRS FATCA summary, 'Reporting thresholds' section
findings.note: 'Living abroad' requires tax home abroad plus 330-day presence per the page. Form 3520 thresholds asserted elsewhere in the repo were NOT verified here (FL02).

findings.topic: US foreign tax credit vs exclusion
findings.claim: US citizens may claim a foreign tax credit (Form 1116) for qualifying foreign income taxes instead of an itemized deduction; no credit is allowed for tax on income excluded under the foreign earned income exclusion; where a treaty reduces the foreign tax rate, only the reduced amount qualifies for the credit.
findings.locator: IRS 'Foreign Tax Credit' page sections 'Qualifying foreign taxes', 'Compliance issues'
findings.note: FEIE and FTC are alternatives with interactions — choosing between them is a personal tax computation not performed here.

findings.claim: The US–China income tax treaty (in force since 1 January 1987) caps source-state tax on dividends, interest and royalties at 10% of the gross amount in each case (for beneficial owners), and the residence state gives credit for the other state's tax; a saving clause sits in Protocol 1.
findings.locator: Treaty Arts. 9, 10, 11, 22; Letter of Submittal; Protocol 1 saving clause
findings.note: Treaty rates matter for investment-type income, not for the FX conversion itself.

findings.claim: There is no legal limit on how much currency or monetary instruments a traveler may carry into or out of the United States, but amounts of $10,000 or greater (combined) must be reported to CBP on FinCEN Form 105 (electronic filing at fincen105.cbp.dhs.gov); non-reporting risks seizure plus civil and/or criminal penalties (31 USC 5316).
findings.locator: CBP official releases (S14 2025; corroborating S15 2017)
findings.note: Filing the report is not a tax and not a limit. Deliberately structuring carry amounts to avoid the report is separately prohibited.

findings.locator: Tariff items 2.2.4.1 and 2.2.4.2; remarks; Important Note 7
findings.note: Bank tariff = commercial primary source, labelled as such. Eligibility for any particular customer segment is account-specific and unverified (FL05). The legacy 'USD 0–7 same-name Global Transfer' claim remains flagged by earlier audits (FL06).

findings.note: Left blank on purpose (FL01, FL08). Obtain a current executable all-in quote (rate, sender fee, cable, correspondent and recipient charges) from the bank before relying on any modeled band.

findings.note: Left blank on purpose (FL01). The HSBC 'Pay Exact' remark confirms third-party charges exist but does not quantify them.

flags.detail: Hui Fa [2007] No. 1 Art. 31 states a USD 5,000 same-day FX cash deposit threshold; Hui Fa [2020] No. 14 Art. 87 states USD 10,000; the 2020 notice says prior inconsistent provisions are governed by it. Verified as a documentation chain (V10); the operating bank's actual threshold should still be confirmed at the counter.
